jobs.description:
Are you ready to bring your innovative perspective and creative skills to ASAA ABLOY Business Segment Pedestrian (BSP) within the ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems? Join our team in Landskrona, Sweden and enjoy a collaborative culture that empowers you to build a career you can be proud of.
 
What would you do as our Product Owner Revolving Doors.
 
As Product Owner for our Revolving Door product range, you assume full technical ownership of a comprehensive and established product line. Coordinating a multidisciplinary R&D team spanning hardware, firmware, and mechanical engineering, you will set priorities, drive alignment with portfolio priorities, and create the conditions in which engineers can perform and grow at their best.
 
This position is well suited to a technically grounded person who combines hands-on engineering insight with the ability to coach a team, manage complexity, and drive results with discipline and clarity.
The role reports to Head of Security Entrance Control and Revolving Doors, and works closely with senior stakeholders across product management, manufacturing, quality, and global ASSA ABLOY divisions to drive innovation, performance, and long-term business impact.
 
You would also:
 
Oversee and develop a multidisciplinary R&D team — provide clear direction and hands-on management of hardware, firmware, and mechanical engineers; foster a culture of technical excellence, structured problem-solving, and continuous professional development, while coaching the team toward stronger resolution-making and greater ownership.
Own the full product development lifecycle — drive concept, validation, industrialisation, and ongoing lifecycle improvements, while ensuring consistent adherence to applicable safety and quality standards, including ISO, CE, EN16005, and UL.
Define and execute the R&D strategy — establish the product roadmap, ensure alignment with broader portfolio and business targets, manage R&D resources, budgets, and timelines, and embed sustainability principles across all stages of product development.
Drive innovation and the adoption of emerging technologies — identify opportunities to enhance product performance and design, stimulate creative thinking within the team, and evaluate the application of IoT, connectivity, AI, and other forward-looking technologies across the product range.
Represent the product externally and manage key stakeholder relationships — act as a credible technical ambassador in customer meetings, trade shows, and industry forums, while maintaining strong internal alignment with segment management, commercial product managers, and factory teams.

 
 
The skills and experience you need
 
We are looking for someone who has:
 
Engineering foundation — a degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related field, combined with a solid background in R&D for electromechanical products gained through hands-on engineering, product development, or early-career coordination roles.
Product lifecycle expertise — demonstrated experience managing the full development lifecycle, from concept and validation through to industrialisation and continuous improvement, with a strong understanding of systems, spare parts, and lifecycle stewardship.
Technical guidance skills— proven ability to lead and coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams, with the capacity to set direction, manage priorities, and drive delivery across hardware, firmware, and mechanical disciplines.
Compliance and quality awareness — familiarity with relevant safety and quality standards such as ISO, CE, EN16005, and UL, and a structured approach to process optimisation and regulatory adherence.
Domain knowledge and technology acumen — familiarity with revolving doors, door mechanics, drive systems, sensors, or embedded control units is a strong advantage. We equally welcome candidates who bring technical curiosity, analytical strength, and the motivation to grow into a product ownership role. An interest in emerging technologies such as IoT, connectivity, and AI is highly valued.

 
You are a natural leader who guides with clarity and purpose — someone who inspires confidence in a team not through authority alone, but through genuine engagement, consistent follow-through, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves when it matters. You think in possibilities, approaching technical tasks with creativity and a structured mind, always looking for smarter ways forward.
 
You are customer-centric by nature, with a keen sense of how engineering decisions translate into real-world impact — both for end users and for the business. You balance technical depth with pragmatic judgement, knowing when to dive into the details and when to step back and see the bigger picture. Proficiency in spoken and written English and Swedish is essential. Additional languages are a welcome advantage.
 
Above all, you act with integrity. You take ownership of your work and your team's outcomes, bring a safety-conscious mindset to every resolution, and hold yourself accountable to the highest standards — commercially, technically, and as a supervisor of people.
 
What we offer
 
We’re passionate about providing amazing opportunities and benefits, so you can continue and progress a lifelong career with us – here’s what we have to offer:
 
Learning and career development opportunities, whether it’s online learning, management training or enhancing your skills
A competitive salary and incentive schemes

 
 
We review applications regularly, so don’t wait
 
We are building diverse, inclusive teams, and encourage applications from everyone who can see themselves working with us. Just set up your profile and apply here.
 
To make sure your personal data is safe, we don’t look at any applications sent by email or post. If you have any questions about the role or the process, email Mona Yusefi Talent Acquisition Business Partner, at mona.yusefi@assaabloy.com.
 
Depending on the risk profile for the role, a background screening will need to be performed. Final candidates may therefore be subjected to a background screening. The performance of the background check is subject to consent and based on our Applicant Privacy Notice.
 
 
Let’s create a safer and more open world - together!
 
To find out more about us, visit www.assaabloy.com

What we do at Blykalla
Blykalla is a Swedish deep-tech company at the forefront of the nuclear industry, pioneering the development of small modular reactors that provide clean, safe, and reliable energy. Thanks to lead-cooling, we achieve high safety in a very compact format, allowing for a simple and cost-effective design that can be mass-produced. Our unique reactor design will provide safe and green baseload energy that perfectly complements solar and wind power.

What you’ll get to do
We are seeking a Senior Control Systems Engineer with deep expertise in ABB 800xA DCS to lead the development of Blykalla's plant control system architecture and implementation strategy.
This is a unique opportunity to help define the control philosophy of a first-of-a-kind advanced nuclear reactor. You will play a key role in ensuring that Blykalla develops and retains ownership of critical control system intellectual property while working closely with ABB and other suppliers.

Key Responsibilities
DCS Architecture & Ownership
Lead the design and development of Blykalla's plant-wide automation and control system architecture.
Define the ABB 800xA system architecture for reactor, balance-of-plant, auxiliary, and test facility applications.
Develop internal engineering standards, libraries, templates, and control strategies to maximize in-house ownership of intellectual property.
Establish long-term governance for control system design, lifecycle management, cybersecurity, and configuration control.

Control System Engineering
Develop functional specifications, control narratives, cause-and-effect matrices, and automation philosophies.
Design and implement control logic, sequences, interlocks, alarms, and operator interfaces.
Configure ABB 800xA applications, controllers, engineering environments, and HMI systems.
Define communication architectures including OPC UA, IEC 61850, Modbus, Profibus/Profinet, Ethernet/IP, and other industrial protocols.
Develop and maintain simulation and testing environments for control system validation.

Nuclear Plant Integration
Support the integration of reactor systems, safety systems, and balance-of-plant equipment into the overall control architecture.
Work closely with reactor, thermal-hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, and safety engineers to define system requirements.
Contribute to licensing and regulatory documentation related to instrumentation and control systems.
Support development of digital I&C architectures aligned with nuclear industry expectations and international standards.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management
Act as the primary technical interface with ABB regarding 800xA architecture, licensing, engineering tools, and implementation support.
Ensure that Blykalla retains ownership of application software, engineering databases, configuration standards, and control strategies.
Manage external engineering partners and system integrators where required.
Participate in factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT), commissioning, and startup activities.

Verification & Validation
Develop testing methodologies for control logic verification and system validation.
Lead integration testing and commissioning activities.
Support development of digital twins and operator training simulators.
Ensure traceability from requirements through implementation and testing.

Who you’ll get to work with
The Senior Control Systems Engineer sits in the Plant engineering Team within Blykalla. We are a diverse team that is passionate about our work and Blykalla. 
Who you are
You will be part of a highly skilled team with a can-do attitude. We value personnel chemistry and strive to create a workplace where you enjoy coming to. There are however a few things that we think will help in order for you to succeed in this role, these are:
MSc or BSc in Control Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years of experience in industrial automation and control systems engineering.
Extensive hands-on experience with ABB 800xA DCS engineering, configuration, commissioning, and lifecycle management.
Proven experience designing and implementing large-scale DCS architectures.
Experience developing control strategies for complex industrial facilities.
Strong understanding of industrial networks, field instrumentation, and process control.
Fluent in English, spoken and written
Fluency in Swedish is a plus

Technical Skills
Expert-level knowledge of ABB 800xA:
AC 800M controllers
Control Builder
Aspect Objects
System 800xA Engineering
Operator Workplace
Alarm Management
Batch and Advanced Process Control (desirable)
Strong understanding of:
ISA-88
ISA-95
IEC 61511
IEC 61508
Industrial cybersecurity principles
Configuration management and software lifecycle practices
Experience with simulation and testing environments.

Location 
This position is for our office in Stockholm.

Reference & Background Checks
As part of our recruitment process, we conduct background checks on all candidates. We may also conduct reference checks to gain a well-rounded understanding of your professional experience, performance, and ways of working. This includes both references provided by you and, where relevant, conversations with other professional contacts who have worked closely with you. We strive to be transparent about our reference-checking process and handle all personal data in accordance with applicable data protection regulations. Any additional references will be sought with professional judgment and only when considered relevant to the role.
We offer competitive compensation aligned with our internal salary framework and growth potential in the role.
We do not accept applications via email. 
We are not open to external help from recruitment agencies.
 
Note on AI Use: Blykalla may use AI technology to assist with certain administrative aspects of the hiring process, such as note-taking, interview documentation, and reporting. However, every resume and application is reviewed directly by our recruiting team. AI tools are used solely for operational support and do not influence candidate evaluation or hiring decisions.
Öppen för alla
Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.

Job Description
WHAT YOU’LL DO 
As Social Producer, you’ll take ownership of social and creator-led productions from brief to final delivery. You’ll turn creative ideas into clear, effective production plans and bring together the right creators, talent, production partners and suppliers to make them happen. 
Working across both fastmoving social content and larger campaign activations, you’ll create flexible production set-ups that allow ideas to come to life at speed without compromising quality or creative intent. You’ll be an important link between creative development and execution, helping ensure our content is relevant for the platform, audience and brand. 
Key responsibilities include 
Lead end-to-end production of social-first and creator-led content, from brief and planning to final asset delivery. 
Translate creative concepts into clear and actionable production plans while protecting the original creative vision. 
Source, negotiate with, contract and manage creators, talent, production partners and other external suppliers. 
Plan and book productions, managing budgets, timelines, contracts, resources and deliverables. 
Manage both smaller, agile creator-led productions and larger social campaign activations. 
Partner closely with creative teams to anticipate production needs and enable strong creative decision-making. 
Ensure content and assets are produced with relevant social platforms, formats and requirements in mind. 
Build flexible and scalable production approaches that support both planned and reactive content creation. 
Continuously identify new partners, production models and ways of working that improve efficiency, speed and relevance. 
Proactively identify and solve production challenges while maintaining a smooth process for everyone involved. 

WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH 
You’ll work closely with creatives and other colleagues across social and creator marketing, turning creative concepts into high-quality content and executions. You’ll also collaborate with creators, talent, agencies, production partners and suppliers, acting as a key connection between creative ambition and production delivery.  
This is a collaborative role where you’ll need to build strong relationships while feeling confident taking ownership and moving productions forward independently. 
WHO YOU ARE 
You’re an experienced producer who knows how to bring creative ideas to life. You combine strong production expertise with an understanding of social content, creators and the realities of producing content for fast-moving digital channels. 
You don’t need every answer from day one. What matters is that you have strong production judgement, understand what a creative idea needs to succeed and know how to find the right people and solutions to make it happen.  
We are looking for people with… 
Strong experience in content production, with relevant experience producing social-first, digital or creator-led content. 
Proven experience independently managing productions from brief through to final delivery. 
Experience working directly with creators, talent, production partners and suppliers. 
Experience with sourcing, negotiation, contracting, budgets, timelines and production planning. 
An understanding of social platforms and how production requirements can differ across channels such as TikTok and Instagram. 
The ability to translate creative concepts into practical production plans without losing the creative intent. 
Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills. 
An understanding of how to balance creative ambition, commercial considerations, quality, speed and efficiency. 

 And people who are… 
Independent and comfortable taking ownership from start to finish. 
Highly organized, solution-oriented and able to manage several moving parts at once. 
Curious about social media, creator culture and evolving ways of producing content. 
Collaborative and strong at building relationships across creative and commercial teams. 
Flexible and comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where not everything is defined from the start. 
Confident challenging established ways of working and exploring new production models. 
Equipped with strong creative judgement and an eye for culturally and socially relevant content. 

WHO WE ARE 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make. 
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. 
WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE 
At H&M Group, you’ll be part of an international and collaborative environment where your ideas and perspectives matter. Alongside opportunities to learn, develop and build your career across H&M Group, we offer a range of benefits. 
Your H&M Group benefits include: 
Employee discount: As an H&M Group employee, you receive an employee discount across eligible H&M Group brands, in stores and online where applicable. Brands include H&M, H&M HOME, H&M Move, COS, Monki, Weekday, & Other Stories and ARKET. 
H&M Incentive Program (HIP). 
Wellbeing allowance: Employees in Sweden receive an annual wellbeing allowance, supporting activities that contribute to health and wellbeing. 

JOIN US 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things - our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are. 
Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here. 
This is a permanent position based in Stockholm, Sweden. Apply as soon as possible by submitting your CV and portfolio in English. 
Due to data privacy regulations, we only accept applications through our career page. 
We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency.We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.

jobs.description:
Are you an experienced payment sales professional ready to combine commercial leadership with closing strategic deals yourself? Dintero is looking for a Head of Enterprise & Platforms Nordics to bring together its Nordic enterprise sales efforts, develop the team and drive growth across some of the company’s most important customer segments.
About the job
This is a direct recruitment, which means that the recruitment process takes place through Bravura and you are employed directly by Dintero.
About the company
Dintero is a fast-growing Norwegian fintech company challenging traditional payment providers with a modern, fully integrated payment platform. The company is one of few players in the Nordics covering the entire payment value chain and is licensed to process Visa and Mastercard transactions directly, making Dintero Norway’s first new acquirer in more than 20 years.
The offering covers online and in-store payments, Unified Commerce and payment solutions for platforms and marketplaces. With enterprise customers such as Vy and regulatory approval to offer payment services across the EEA, Dintero is positioned for further expansion across the Nordics and Europe. In 2025, the company onboarded more than 2,100 new businesses, increased payment volume by over 150% and revenue by 200%, while reaching profitability in Q4.
You will join a growing Nordic organisation with short decision paths and a high degree of ownership. There are established structures and processes, but these evolve as the business grows. Leaders are expected to identify what can be improved and actively contribute to developing how the organisation works.
Tasks and responsibilities
As Head of Enterprise & Platforms Nordics, you will have commercial responsibility for developing Dintero’s enterprise and platform sales across Sweden, Norway and Denmark. A key part of the role is to bring the three markets together and establish a common Nordic approach to sales, pipeline management and commercial priorities.
This is a player-coach role, particularly during the first year. Alongside leading and developing the team, you will personally work with Dintero’s most strategic customers and drive complex enterprise opportunities from initial dialogue to signed agreement. You will work with senior and C-level decision-makers and navigate longer sales cycles involving both commercial and technical stakeholders.
You will also develop the existing sales team and play an active role in recruiting and building the team further across the Nordics, with the ambition to hire 3–5 additional salespeople during the first 12 months. As the organisation expands, the role will gradually shift towards more leadership and commercial strategy, while maintaining a strong connection to customers and the market.
You will work closely with the CEO, product and technical teams to develop Dintero’s enterprise offering. You are not expected to be a technical specialist, but you need to understand complex payment solutions and be comfortable discussing areas such as APIs, integrations and platform architecture.
Your main responsibilities include:

Lead and develop Enterprise & Platforms sales across the Nordics

Personally drive and close strategic enterprise and platform deals

Coach and develop the existing sales team and recruit additional salespeople

Develop structure around pipeline, sales methodology, CRM and forecasting

Collaborate with leadership, product and technical teams to develop the enterprise offering

Education, experience and personal characteristics
Several years of experience within the payments industry

Proven experience closing complex, high-value enterprise deals in the Nordic market

Previous leadership experience, including people responsibility, coaching, developing and recruiting salespeople

Experience selling both in-store terminal solutions and online/e-commerce payments

Commercial and technical understanding of areas such as APIs and integrations and platform architecture

Existing network within Nordic enterprise retail

Fluent English and at least one Scandinavian language: Swedish, Norwegian or Danish

Experience selling through and building partnerships with e-commerce platforms and integration partners is meritorious

An existing network across marketplace or platform verticals is meritorious

To succeed in the role, you take ownership and are comfortable creating structure while remaining close to sales. As a leader, you coach and give experienced salespeople ownership of their deals while setting clear expectations around execution and results.
You are comfortable in an environment where processes evolve as the company grows. Rather than simply working within an existing structure, you identify what could work better and take initiative to change it. You are also curious and able to quickly understand complex technical and commercial topics, even when you do not have all the answers from the start.
Other information
Start: Upon agreement  Location: Stockholm, Oslo or Copenhagen. If based outside Oslo, regular travel to the Oslo office is expected.  Salary: Upon agreement

#Specialist

Ovako is one of Europe’s leading manufacturers of advanced engineering steel and has supplied steel for critical industrial applications for nearly 500 years. The company is now making a strategic investment in the defence industry and is looking for someone who wants to play a key role in establishing and developing Ovako’s position in one of Europe’s fastest-growing segments.
At Ovako, you will have the opportunity to combine business development, an understanding of the defence industry and relationship building in a role offering substantial autonomy, high visibility and the opportunity to shape the direction of an entirely new initiative. You will join a stable industrial company with a long-term perspective, Nordic production, strong ownership and a clear ambition to grow within the defence segment.
The location is flexible, although we would ideally like you to be based at our sales office in Karlskoga. You may also be based at one of our major production sites in Hofors, Smedjebacken, Boxholm or Hällefors, or at our office in Örebro.
In the role of Sales Manager Security and Defense, you will be responsible for establishing, developing and strengthening Ovako’s business within the defence industry. This is a newly created role designed to develop Ovako’s long-term position throughout the defence supply chain, from OEMs and systems suppliers to subcontractors and other key players in the segment.
At the heart of the role is identifying business opportunities at an early stage, building relationships with the right decision-makers and creating a strong pipeline of future defence business. You will take a strategic approach to mapping the market, projects, decision-making processes and material requirements, while moving commercial discussions forward through customer meetings, quotations, negotiations and long-term relationship development.
To succeed, you need to be comfortable with long sales cycles. You understand how the defence industry operates, know where decisions are made and can build trust with technical specialists, procurement professionals and business leaders alike. The role requires a high degree of independence, and you will be expected to set your own agenda, take the initiative and drive business forward, even when results may take time to materialise.
You will represent the full Ovako Group offering and work closely with the sales organisation, business units, production and R&D to translate customer needs into long-term business opportunities.
We are looking for someone with an established network within the defence industry and existing relationships with relevant players, such as OEMs, systems suppliers, subcontractors or companies in related defence industries. You have experience in sales, business development, procurement or engineering within the defence sector and are accustomed to navigating complex business environments where sales cycles are often long and involve multiple stakeholders.
Experience in the steel industry is an advantage, but what matters most is your understanding of the defence segment, its decision-making processes and how to build long-term business through trust and relationships. Experience in steel, component manufacturing, materials engineering or the manufacturing industry is desirable but not essential.
As a person, you are commercially driven, persistent and proactive. You thrive in a role where you can establish structures, identify opportunities and move activities forward on your own initiative. At the same time, you bring a strategic perspective and the ability to understand the connections between different players throughout the defence supply chain. You naturally build trust, work in a structured way and are motivated by developing business that creates lasting value.
A good command of Swedish and English, together with a category B driving licence, is essential for the role. Ideally, you hold a university qualification in a relevant field or another post-secondary qualification. Travel is part of the role. The location is flexible, although we would ideally like you to be based in central Sweden or be able to visit one of Ovako’s sites regularly.
You will be offered a unique opportunity to help build Ovako’s defence industry initiative from the ground up. The role has strong support from management and Group management and gives you the opportunity to make your mark on a business area of major strategic importance to the company.
Ovako combines the resources of a large industrial company with a culture where individuals make a difference. You will have autonomy and responsibility, strong support from colleagues and the opportunity to influence both the development of the business and your own professional growth. You will join a global organisation with strong industrial owners, Nordic production and a long tradition of innovation, quality and sustainability.
We welcome your application today. Applications are reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis. Please submit your application below, as we do not accept applications through any other channel. If you would like to learn more about the role, please contact Made for Sales.
About Ovako
Ovako is a leading European manufacturer of engineering steel for customers in sectors including industry, energy, mining and automotive, as well as defence-related applications. The company has approximately 2,500 employees, annual revenue of approximately EUR 1 billion and production facilities in Sweden and Finland. Drawing on extensive industrial experience, strong materials expertise and a clear focus on sustainability, Ovako develops advanced steel solutions for some of the world’s most demanding applications. The company is part of the Nippon Steel Group through Sanyo Special Steel and has a long-term industrial owner with a strong focus on innovation and future growth.

About us
Danieli Morgårdshammar AB is part of the international Danieli Group and has been serving the Nordic metals industry for more than 170 years. Based in Smedjebacken, Sweden, we support steel, aluminum and other metal producers throughout Scandinavia with engineering services, spare parts, technical support and long-term partnership solutions.

We operate in an industry where trust, competence and personal relationships are often more important than presentations, marketing materials or corporate references. Our success is built on credibility and on being recognized as a reliable partner by the people who operate and maintain production facilities every day.
 
Responsibilities
We are looking for an experienced industry professional who already understands the reality of steel mills, rolling mills and metal processing plants.
This is not a typical sales position, more a business developer position.
The ideal candidate is someone who has worked directly within the metals industry or closely alongside plant personnel and understands how industrial decisions are truly made. Candidates coming directly from steel, aluminum or other metals production facilities are particularly encouraged to apply.
The primary focus of this role is the development of Danieli aftermarket and service business.
Activities include the sales, coordination, and follow-up of the following services and solutions for your designated customers:
Spare Parts Supply
Technical Services
On-site Assistance
Maintenance Support
Roll Shop Solutions
Equipment Refurbishments
Small and Medium Revamping Projects
Plant Modernizations and Upgrades
Engineering and Technical Consulting

Success in this role requires the ability to understand customers' operational challenges and identify opportunities where Danieli's technical expertise and service capabilities can create measurable value.
Technical Requirements
We are particularly interested in candidates who have:
Previous experience in the steel, aluminum or metals industry.
Direct experience working in or closely with production plants, rolling mills, maintenance organizations or technical departments.
Existing professional relationships within the Nordic metals industry.
A strong understanding of industrial operations, maintenance and production environments.
Experience interacting with: Roll Shop Managers; Production Managers; Maintenance Managers; Foremen and Supervisors; Category Managers; Purchasing Departments; Technical Specialists.

More than technical qualifications, we are looking for someone who understands plant culture, speaks the language of industrial operations and can quickly establish credibility with the people who influence purchasing decisions.
Fluent English, written and spoken, mother language Swedish.
Willingness to travel throughout the Nordic countries.
Valid driving license.
Experience with CRM systems (but not as a primary focus)
Technical education or equivalent industry experience is considered an advantage.

Soft Skills
For this position, interpersonal capabilities are just as important as technical knowledge.
The successful candidate will:
Build trust naturally and quickly.
Be highly relationship-driven and people-oriented.
Communicate confidently with personnel at all organizational levels.
Be proactive, decisive and commercially minded.
Feel comfortable opening doors and creating opportunities from scratch.
Demonstrate strong ownership and initiative.
Possess the credibility and character required to earn customers' confidence over time.
Be capable of transforming an initial contact into a long-term business partnership.

In the Nordic business culture, trust is often the primary factor behind purchasing decisions. We therefore place exceptional importance on integrity, credibility and relationship-building skills.
Other
Danieli - Morgårdshammar and the Danieli Group are already well known throughout the Nordic metals industry. Significant efforts have been made in recent years to increase our presence within production facilities, establish direct contacts with key stakeholders and strengthen our reputation across the region.
Several customers already work with Danieli. However, substantial opportunities remain to deepen those relationships and expand our involvement far beyond our current level of business.
Your mission will be to transform existing awareness into trust, and trust into long-term partnerships, customer loyalty and sustainable business growth.
We are looking for someone who can become the person our customers call first when they need advice, support or a reliable partner.
The successful candidate will not operate as a stand-alone salesperson.
Commercial strategy, customer development plans and growth initiatives are defined in close coordination with the Danieli Group headquarters in Italy and the Nordic Area.
The role is fully integrated within a broader international organization and supported by dedicated technical, commercial and engineering resources worldwide.
Daily support is provided by the Nordic Area Manager, while customer visits and business development activities are frequently performed jointly with Product Line Managers, technical specialists and senior representatives from Danieli headquarters.
The objective is to combine local presence and relationship-building with the engineering expertise, product knowledge and global resources of the Danieli Group. We are therefore looking for a person who enjoys being on the front line with customers, while being fully supported by an international team behind them.
You are not expected to be a lone hunter searching for orders.
We are looking for someone who can walk into a plant, understand the challenges faced by its people, speak their language and ultimately become the person they trust when it is time to place an order.
In the Nordic industrial culture, trust is not a sales tool, It is the foundation upon which long-term business is built.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before the closing date. Interviews are conducted continuously throughout the recruitment process. Preferred start date is as soon as possible, but this is not a requirement.
Morgårdshammar AB is a member of Teknikföretagen and applies the relevant collective bargaining agreements within the Swedish engineering industry, including the Technology Agreement (Teknikavtalet).

XBP Europe is an innovative, forward-thinking provider of bills and payment process solutions. Leveraging an EMEA-wide footprint and proprietary technology and services, we are backed by decades of industry-relevant experience.

Bills and payment processes are increasingly omni-channel and paperless. That’s where XBP Europe comes in. Our offerings enable seamless workflows and frictionless transactions. XBP Europe combines physical documents, digital data, and instant messaging to help organisations work smarter. As part of that, we help to gather, process, and refine valuable data for use in decision-making.

Our digital transformation solutions enhance efficiency, cash flow, and end-user experience. We serve a growing client list throughout Europe. See why organisations of all sizes choose XBP Europe as a digital transformation partner, visit our website at www.xbpeurope.com

You will belong to the Supply Data & Analytics team, reporting to the Data & Analytics Manager. We are enabling data democratisation through scalable self-service capabilities and AI enablement, while ensuring high quality, timely and cost efficient data products that support IKEA Supply in making more informed and effective business decisions.
Job Description
As Team Manager you will lead our Data Scientist competence hub, a home for people who share a craft, and in the future the role may extend to include other roles too. Our Data & Analytics team works in a product operating model: cross-functional data product teams, guided by product leaders, own and continuously improve data products that create lasting value for IKEA Supply. The product teams own what is built and why; you own the people and the craft, making sure your team members are motivated, growing and set up to do great work in those teams. Your most important job is to be a great manager. You will also be a trusted technical guide for the team on methods, quality and good practice, and collaborate closely with product owners, Data & Digital Product Leaders and stakeholders across IKEA Supply.
In this role, your typical week can look something like this:
Leading, coaching and developing your team members through regular one-to-ones, feedback, career conversations and clear expectations, creating a safe and inclusive team culture.
Taking care of recruitment, onboarding, competence development and succession planning for your competence hub.
Making sure your Data Scientists are well placed in cross-functional data product teams, partnering with product owners on priorities and capacity, and removing blockers so the team can deliver value continuously.
Providing technical leadership for the Data Scientists, supporting sound modelling, statistics, machine learning and experimentation practices, and making sure quality is built into every deliverable.
Making sure insights and conclusions from data science are clear, trusted and easily available to business stakeholders, and that statistical and machine learning concepts are explained to non-technical audiences.
Collaborating with data engineers, analysts, architects and peers to ensure consistent methodologies, tools and ways of working across Supply Data & Analytics and the wider IKEA data community.
Supporting responsible use of AI and AI assisted tools in data science work, and keeping up to date with technology trends and business needs.
Contributing to planning and budgeting by providing input on resources, development and investment needs.

Qualifications
What we'd like you to bring to the table
The role as a Team Manager is a good match if you bring:
Direct or indirect people management experience: leading people to perform and deliver, developing competence, recruiting and planning succession. Strong people skills, empathy and a coaching mindset are what matter most.
A genuine passion for building inclusive, high-trust teams where people feel safe to grow, make mistakes and learn from them.
Strong technical background in data science or similar, with experience developing data driven products for real-life business problems, and the ability to guide Data Scientists on approach and quality.
Experience in understanding business needs and turning them into data products that deliver measurable value, in close collaboration with product leaders.
The ability to clearly communicate statistical and machine learning concepts to non-technical audiences and to build strong relationships with stakeholders and product owners.
Experience working in a product operating model and in an agile set-up, with an understanding of data product principles such as iterative delivery, ownership and continuous improvement.
A bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or a related quantitative field; an advanced degree is preferred.

It's a plus if you also have:
Experience leading data science teams in a large enterprise or complex matrixed organisation, ideally within supply chain, logistics or manufacturing.
Experience leading teams within a product operating model, partnering with Data & Digital Product Leaders or equivalent.
Experience introducing common ways of working, tools and competence in the business.
Experience with budgeting and resource planning.
Experience applying generative AI or agent based workflows in data science.
Experience leading or growing several different roles or competence areas within data and analytics.

Additional information
This team is located in Malmö, Sweden. We regret that we are unable to handle applications made by e-mail. We only handle applications in English. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible, but no later than 15th Dec. 2026. Ensure that you include your CV and Motivation Letter.
At IKEA, we are looking for people who believe everyone deserves a seat at the table. You're welcome no matter where you come from, what you believe and what you look like. We don't even care how you have furnished your home. We're interested in you simply because you're you. Even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. We believe that people's different perspectives, backgrounds and personalities make us better at understanding our customers' dreams and needs. If you have a special need that requires accommodation in the recruitment process, just let us know.
We are looking forward to hearing from you soon!

We'll give you opportunities to work on some of the most ambitious and exciting projects currently being designed and developed in the built environment sector. 
You'll continue to learn and advance as everyone who works for us is provided with a tailored training programme. Our mentoring and reverse mentoring schemes will enable you to share your expertise while gaining fresh insights. 
What makes RLB unique is our inclusive culture. As an independent, employee-owned business, teamwork and collaboration lies at the heart of everything we do. Hybrid and flexible working arrangements and family-friendly policies are just some of the ways we invest in employee wellbeing. 
Join us and you will thrive personally as well as professionally.

Candidate Profile

Strong communication and organizational skills.

Fluent in English (both verbal and written communication).

RLB Employee Benefits

About the role
Imagine HR where efficient, trusted processes and AI go hand in hand: smooth onboarding, people data everyone can trust, and reliable AI answers to everyday questions about how we work. As our AI-Driven HR Operations Specialist, you make that happen. You design, document, and automate our core HR processes, and you put AI to work wherever it does the job better, so managers and employees across Tacton spend less time on admin and more time on what matters. This is the role for someone who thinks in processes, rules, and data flows, gets a real buzz from what AI can do, and wants to turn that into everyday impact.
You'll report directly to Eva Lessing, our CHRO, and team up with the HR team, our AI Automation Specialist, IT, and Security and Compliance to bring your ideas to life.
What you will do
• Build the HR automation and AI roadmap, prioritizing by business value, process readiness, data sensitivity, and effort, and choosing between automation, AI, or leaving a process as it is. Then build and run the solutions that make HR work smarter for everyone at Tacton.

• Make sure every solution meets our security and privacy requirements, including ISO 27001 and SOC 2.

What we are looking for
• 5+ years in HR, ideally in HR operations, HR systems, or HR technology, with hands-on experience designing and automating HR processes and a solid understanding of people data.
• A genuine curiosity and passion for what AI can do, backed by hands-on experience with AI tools such as Claude (our main AI tool at Tacton), ChatGPT, or Microsoft Copilot, including AI and automation solutions you have built and maintained, such as workflows and assistants, with measurable results.

Your first six months

• Agree a roadmap with priorities and baseline measures.

Why join us

• Your expertise matters from day one. Our HR team already uses AI and is eager to do more, but we need an expert to lead the way. You will raise the bar for all of us, and because the need is big, your work will be seen and truly appreciated.
• Your impact reaches the whole company. Every process you simplify saves time and increases quality for employees and managers in every country we operate in.
• You have room to move fast. You report to our CHRO, who sees her job as removing obstacles for you. You join an engaged HR team of six in Stockholm, Chicago, and Karlsruhe that loves trying new things.
• You grow with a company on the move. Tacton develops every day and is expanding from a single product into a full platform, so the role grows as you grow.
What to expect during the recruitment process
• Screening call with Global Talent Acquisition Partner
• First interview with our hiring manager
• Personality and logical ability test
• Second interview and peer meeting, which will include a case
• Interview with senior management
• Reference checks
• Background checks
What we offer
At Tacton, you'll develop your career in an organization that values teamwork and promotes individual growth. We offer a global and open environment, working with the latest technology to solve important and complex problems in the manufacturing industry.
• Flexible hybrid setup: 3 days a week in the office.
• 33 days of paid time off: 30 vacation days plus 3 extra to make sure you get the rest you deserve.
• Premium occupational pension: Our pension plan goes beyond ITP1, with higher employer contributions depending on your age and salary level.

Promise what you can build. Build what you promised. For 26 years, Tacton has helped manufacturers of complex products around the world do exactly that. Boliden is a high-tech metals company with its own mines and smelters that works long-term to guarantee society's access to base and precious metals. For a century, our work has been part of the value chains that have shaped modern society. At Boliden, we know that the metals we mine and make available will continue to play a crucial role in the future – what matters is how we produce them. Become a part of us and drive change for generations to come. 
 
Your opportunity
Technology is transforming the metals industry, creating new opportunities to improve safety, sustainability, productivity, and business performance. 
As Head of IT Smelters, you will play a key role in shaping the digital future of Boliden's Smelter operations. In this highly visible leadership position, you will drive the technology strategy, lead business-critical transformation initiatives, and ensure that digital solutions create lasting value across one of Europe's leading metals companies.

Drive digital transformation, innovation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Ensure secure, reliable, and cost-effective IT services and solutions. 
Collaborate across Group IT and business functions to balance local needs with enterprise-wide priorities. 
Contribute to the broader IT leadership agenda and the long-term development of Boliden's technology landscape.

 
What you bring
You are a strategic and business-oriented IT leader with a passion for technology, transformation, and people leadership. You build strong relationships across the organization, drive change, and translate business needs into technology-enabled value.
Required qualifications:
Extensive experience in senior IT leadership roles, with a proven ability to lead leaders, build high-performing teams, and influence stakeholders in complex matrix organizations.
Strong track record of driving digital transformation and change. 
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior business leaders and translate business strategy into technology priorities.
Good understanding of IT governance, portfolio management, budgeting, and vendor management. 
Experience delivering secure and reliable IT services.

jobs.description:
Do you want to run a platform as a product, with developers as your customers?

Our mission is to enable our DevOps teams to focus on building great applications by providing a shared internal developer platform, tools, templates and ways of working that simplify the entire software development lifecycle. Today, we support more than 20 teams across all three divisions, combining hands-on engineering with coaching, training and technical enablement.

Ultimately, our goal is simple: remove complexity, create great developer experiences and enable teams to deliver secure, high-quality software faster.

Role Description
CORE Platform gives our DevOps teams a paved road to build, test, deploy and observe software safely and efficiently. Our ambition is to create a platform that teams choose because it makes their work easier, not simply because they have to use it.

As Platform Product Manager, you will treat the platform as a product, with developers as your customers. You will stay close to our DevOps teams, understand their needs and use feedback and data to shape priorities, set goals and build a roadmap focused on outcomes rather than output.

Working closely with domain leads and platform engineers, you will help ensure CORE Platform feels like one coherent developer experience rather than a collection of tools. You will connect technical platform development with the wider needs of Husqvarna Group, helping us invest where we can create the greatest value for both developers and the business.

Looking ahead, we are also preparing for AI agents to become platform users alongside developers. You will help shape what this means for the platform and how it influences our future priorities. What you will do:

Shape the platform strategy and roadmap based on user needs, business priorities and measurable outcomes.
Work closely with developers to understand their needs, test ideas early and create effective feedback loops.
Translate developer and business needs into clear platform priorities.
Define and follow up on goals and metrics around adoption, developer experience and platform value.
Work with domain leads and platform engineers to create a consistent and coherent platform experience.
Continuously evaluate whether the platform is solving the right problems and be ready to evolve, start or stop initiatives based on data and feedback.
Connect platform development to the wider business context and ensure investments create meaningful value for Husqvarna Group.

Your profile
Beyond your experience, you are genuinely curious about your users and approach product development with an outcome-focused and adaptable mindset. You understand that a platform is never finished and are comfortable changing direction as user needs, business priorities and technology evolve.
 
You see the bigger picture and can balance the needs of developers with the value we want to create for the business. You are confident in setting priorities and saying no when needed, while being able to clearly explain the reasoning behind your decisions, regardless of who you are speaking with.
 
You are also curious about the opportunities AI brings to software development, while maintaining a pragmatic view of where it creates real value. Most importantly, you are a humble and collaborative team player who enjoys working with others, brings a sense of humour and cares about succeeding together. We believe you bring:

5+ years of experience working in or closely with software engineering.
A good understanding of the software development lifecycle and DevOps, including how software is built, deployed and operated.
Experience in product management, ideally within a technical or internal product environment.
A strong product mindset, with the ability to translate user and business needs into priorities and measurable outcomes.
Experience defining and using metrics to understand adoption, user experience and the value a product delivers.
Professional proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

 
Experience from Platform Engineering, working with platforms as products, or familiarity with cloud technologies such as AWS, is a plus.
 
Location
Huskvarna. We believe the best ideas happen when we are connected. We spend most of our time together in the office, creating space for collaboration, creativity, and fast decision-making. This is consistent across all our global offices and helps us maintain a strong culture, support learning and development, and ensure everyone has access to the people and resources they need to thrive.

Your application
Please apply with CV and Cover Letter. We do not accept applications via email due to GDPR regulations. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and the position may be filled before the application deadline. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For more questions regarding the position please contact: Hiring Manager: Mathias von Knorring, mathias.von.knorring@husqvarnagroup.com.  For more information about the recruitment process, please contact: Recruiter: Gorjana Dubovina,gorjana.dubovina@husqvarnagroup.com.

Processing of personal data
When you send in your application we will process your personal data. In case we choose to proceed with your application, we may ask you to verify your identity before giving you a job offer. For more information about how we process your personal data, who we may share it with and what rights you have, please see our privacy notice.

Winning Through Culture 
We believe that business is ultimately about people, as a team, we win and grow together. Our culture is built on bold ideas, strong commitment, and a shared purpose, creating an environment where innovation thrives, people grow, and every contribution matters.
 
Our culture is built on three core themes: 
Bold: We push boundaries, embrace challenges, and explore new possibilities.
Dedicated: We put in the hard work, bring passion and resilience to every challenge we take on.
Care: We support each other, consider the impact of our actions, and strive to make a lasting difference. 

 
Whether you’re starting your career or looking for the next big step, we offer a place where passion and purpose come together. Join us in shaping the future! 

Learn more about our culture here.

Join Truecaller – The place where innovation meets impact!
Truecaller's mission is to build trust in communication by making it safer, smarter, and more efficient. Born in Sweden, trusted by the world, and here’s why we stand out:

We are trusted by over 500 million active users every month across 190+ countries
We identify over 15 billion calls daily, helping users avoid spam and scams
We are powered by a team of 400+ employees from 45+ nationalities

We always look for people who take initiative, own their work, and keep raising the bar. An entrepreneurial mindset matters here, especially when it turns bold ideas into real actions. We stay collaborative and focused, always searching for smarter paths forward. If you want to make an impact and grow with a team that inspires millions, you’ll fit right in.
The role 
This is a horizontal role: rather than owning one surface, you set the multi-year product strategy for how Truecaller uses data and decisioning to grow revenue across all of them - Ads, Premium, Business Messaging, and Growth - and decide where the leverage goes next. You will guide the product managers who own individual surfaces, take the strategy to the executive team and win the decisions it needs, and lead through expertise and credibility rather than a reporting line. Expect to spend as much time with commercial and product leadership as with the engineers and data scientists building the systems.
What you'll do
● Set the multi-year product strategy for Revenue Intelligence - one direction across Ads, Premium, Business Messaging and Growth, grounded in user behaviour, revenue data and where the ad and subscription markets are heading.
●  Take that strategy to the executive team and win the decisions it needs - investment, sequencing and what we stop doing.
● Own initiatives that cut across surfaces and platforms - bringing ad-grade targeting to Premium, or a single user-signal layer every surface reads from - and drive the structural calls that affect more than one function.
● Take on problems nobody has framed yet - a new revenue surface, a regulatory shift, a new market - and turn them into a plan with owners, metrics and a decision date.
● Set the bar for measurement: every Revenue Intelligence launch ships with an agreed success metric, a holdout and a clear ship/kill rule.
● Act as advisor to the Revenue Intelligence squads and to the Product Areas that consume them, and coach the product managers around you through reviews, critiques and career guidance.
What you bring in
● 12+ years of product management experience, including several years setting strategy across multiple product areas at Principal level or equivalent.
● Deep expertise in consumer monetization at scale - ad ranking and auctions, targeting, recommendations, subscription conversion, or ML-driven decisioning.
● A track record of influencing executive decisions with well-researched recommendations, and of delivering results across teams you do not manage.
● Fluency with data and experimentation: you write your own SQL, design experiments, and can tell a real causal lift from noise.
● Comfort with the technical substance - retrieval vs. ranking, exploration vs. exploitation, online vs. offline metrics - enough to steer architecture and platform decisions.
● Experience mentoring product managers and raising the craft of a product team.
● Clear, concise writing - your strategy documents carry executive decisions on their own.
It would be great if you also have
● Experience with the India digital advertising market - advertisers, agencies, programmatic demand and DSPs.
● Working knowledge of privacy rules that shape targeting, such as GDPR and India's DPDP Act.
● Product ownership of a data or ML platform used by several product teams.
● Experience shipping AI- or LLM-based product features.

What we offer: 
We support growth through learning resources, leadership programs, mentoring, and real hands-on work. People can move between teams and projects to build new skills and keep things interesting. We offer clear internal mobility and a transparent path for progression, with leaders who stay involved and provide guidance throughout the year. In addition, you will benefit from: 
A comprehensive compensation package: We offer a competitive salary, 30 days of paid vacation, private health insurance, parental leave top-up, pension, and wellness contributions.
Modern tools to do your best work: Choose your preferred computer and phone within our budget, so you can work comfortably and efficiently.
A people-focused office culture: We value in-person collaboration and follow an office-first model, with some flexibility. Our offices offer a vibrant environment with opportunities to learn, connect, and recharge, from breakfast, lunch, and well-stocked snack stations and quiet spaces to team activities such as movie nights, tech meetups, and cultural events. There's something for everyone.
Truecaller’s “Lab Days” offer a space for imagination: 5 times per year for 3 days, where everyone steps away from their normal tasks to explore new, bold ideas and build things they’ve always wanted to. It’s a space where curiosity leads the way, and prototypes take shape. Some concepts even make it into production, and a few have grown into real features used by millions today. Lab Days allow you to be creative, learn fast, and help shape Truecaller's future.

Come as you are:
Truecaller is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe that a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences strengthens our products and our culture. No matter where you're from, what language you speak, or how you identify, we value what makes you unique and would love to get to know you. 
Check out Life at Truecaller - Behind the code: https://www.instagram.com/lifeattruecaller/
Sounds like a great opportunity?
We will fill the position as soon as we find the right candidate, so please send your application as soon as possible. As part of the recruitment process, we will conduct a background check.
We only accept applications in English.

Job ID: 7252
 
Counterparty Credit Risk Model Developer [Senior/Lead Quantitative Risk Analyst] (permanent position)
 
We are looking for a quantitative model developer with an interest in derivatives, risk modelling and practical implementation.
 
About our team
 
Meet the Counterparty Credit Risk Models team. The role combines mathematical finance, Python development and an understanding of trading and regulatory requirements. We welcome candidates with experience in counterparty credit risk or XVA, as well as those with relevant experience in derivatives pricing, quantitative risk or derivative trading.
 
Our team develops and maintains Nordea’s counterparty credit risk exposure models, including the Internal Model Method (IMM). Our work covers the full model lifecycle: interpreting requirements, developing methodologies, sourcing and analysing data, implementing models and supporting validation and regulatory approval.
 
You will work with experienced quantitative colleagues in a friendly and supportive team and collaborate with trading, technology, model validation and risk management. We share expertise across projects, while giving each team member responsibility for taking their work forward.
 
Collaboration. Ownership. Passion. Courage. These are the values that guide us in how we work and how we make decisions – and that we imagine you share with us. 
 
What you’ll be doing
 
Main responsibilities in this role:
Develop and improve counterparty credit risk models, combining sound methodology with practical implementation.
Investigate derivatives pricing and exposure behaviour, and assess the implications of modelling choices for trading portfolios and risk measures.
Source, reconcile and analyse trade and market data from front-office and other internal systems.
